text:
Jonas Weber: kicking off quick quality sanity for the FP8/INT8 sprint. we need something we can run daily w/ the perf matrix so we don’t ship a “fast but wrong” kernel path.

Jonas Weber: ask: can we align today on (a) which prompt sets to use, (b) what metrics are “good enough” for sanity vs full eval, (c) what deltas are acceptable vs baseline.

Arjun Desai: +1. for scope: i’m thinking “sanity suite” != full regression. should catch obvious: JSON/structured output breaks, tool call weirdness, long context drift, and any safety/refusal spikes.

Olivia Grant: agree. if we keep it lightweight + deterministic-ish, we can run per candidate (FP8 attn, INT8 matmul) without blocking perf runs.

Claire Dubois: also: please define up front how we interpret variance. we’ve already got perf variance issues; quality is worse. if we don’t lock seeds / sampling configs, we’ll chase noise.

Priyanka Bose: i can wire this into the eval harness runner we already have. question: which models are “top hosted” in this sprint? i can prep the mapping.

Grace Kim: top 6 from runtime side are: llama-3.1-8b-instruct, llama-3.1-70b-instruct, mixtral-8x7b-instruct, qwen2.5-7b-instruct, qwen2.5-32b-instruct, mistral-large-ish (whatever name in catalog). i’ll drop exact registry IDs when i’m back at laptop.

Rina Kobayashi: from harness perspective: please keep prompts small enough to run on both H100/A100 quickly. our perf suite already has long-context cases; can we sample a *few* long ones but not 100?

Jonas Weber: proposal v0:
- Suite = 120 prompts total, split:
  - 60 “general” from benchmark-suite-v3 (summarization, Q&A, code, reasoning)
  - 20 tool calling (function schema adherence)
  - 20 structured output (JSON + strict schema)
  - 20 long-context (8k-16k input; short output)
- Run configs:
  - temperature=0 for structured + tool calling (deterministic)
  - temperature=0.2 for general (but fixed seed)
  - max_tokens fixed per bucket
- Compare baseline (FP16/BF16 path we ship today) vs candidate (FP8 or INT8)

Claire Dubois: +1 but please specify scoring. “looks good” won’t fly.

Olivia Grant: scoring ideas:
- structured output: JSON parse success rate + schema validation pass rate
- tool calling: exact tool name + required arg keys present + JSON parse
- general: use a cheap LLM-judge? that might be too heavy. alternative: simple reference-based for a subset (rougeL for summaries; exact match for short QA) + a “refusal rate” check.

Arjun Desai: we can do reference-based for a limited set; we already have some goldens for summaries + extraction. for reasoning it’s messy.

Priyanka Bose: we have a “golden prompts + lightweight scoring” set from last quarter (i think ~40). i can blend those in. also if we set temp=0 we can do exact string match on some tasks.

Jonas Weber: for sanity suite, i’d prefer:
- bucket A (structured/tool) strict pass/fail
- bucket B (reference) numeric metrics
- bucket C (freeform) do “semantic similarity” only if easy/cheap

Hiro Tanaka: kernel team request: what thresholds would actually block enablement? we’re going to see small diffs just from sampling.

Claire Dubois: answer: block only on *clear* regressions.
- Any increase in invalid JSON / schema failures above noise is a hard stop.
- For reference metrics: define a minimum delta that’s bigger than run-to-run jitter.
- For long-context: watch for “lost in middle” regressions / truncation / nonsense.

Olivia Grant: we can also track:
- output length distribution shift (if quantization causes early EOS)
- tool call frequency shift
- refusal keyword rate (“I can’t”, “I’m unable”) as a crude proxy

Arjun Desai: thresholds suggestion (sanity):
- structured JSON validity: candidate must be within -0.5pp of baseline; if worse by >=1pp, fail.
- schema pass rate: same.
- tool-call correctness: within -1pp.
- summary rougeL: within -0.5 absolute (or -2% relative) on the subset.
- extraction exact match: within -1pp.
- long-context: no more than +0.5pp “not found / incorrect citation” on the long-context QA subset.

Jonas Weber: that seems reasonable. we should note: if baseline is already <95% JSON-valid, we should treat that as a known issue and not block FP8/INT8. but if we drop further, block.

Rina Kobayashi: how are we going to run this? separate from perf matrix, or as part of matrix runner? i’d rather not mix quality into perf jobs.

Priyanka Bose: i can run it as a nightly job triggered off the same build/container. inputs:
- model id
- kernel_mode (baseline/fp8/int8)
- seed
- prompt set id
outputs:
- per-prompt result json
- aggregate csv

Grace Kim: pls also include “kv-cache alignment edge” case? we saw weirdness on decode for some shapes; might show up as output truncation.

Olivia Grant: i can add a small “decode heavy” bucket: short prompt, long gen (e.g. 512-1024 tokens) for 10 prompts. check for repetition / gibberish.

Claire Dubois: careful: long gen quality scoring is hard. but we can check repetition rate (distinct-ngrams) + “ends with unfinished JSON” for structured ones.

Jonas Weber: ok. updated suite:
- 60 general (mix)
- 20 tool calling
- 20 structured JSON
- 20 long-context short-answer
- +10 decode-heavy (from general, but forced long gen)
(=130)

Talia Benson: timing: can we have v1 by tomorrow EOD? we want it running by the time the first big H100 matrix finishes.

Priyanka Bose: yes if we keep it simple. i’ll base off eval-harness PR-519 (quantization sanity suite). will post a doc w/ exact prompt ids.

EvalBot: Workflow template created: `quant_sanity_v1` (owner: Priyanka Bose).

Arjun Desai: one more thing: INT8 needs calibration sometimes; do we run sanity on both “uncalibrated int8” and “calibrated int8”? otherwise we’ll blame kernels for bad scales.

Priyanka Bose: good call. for sanity, i propose:
- INT8 runs use the current recommended calibration artifacts (if available)
- if missing, run a “best effort” calibration on a small calibration set and label it clearly

Claire Dubois: please label everything. every report should include: model hash, quant profile name, calibration source, runtime build sha.

Grace Kim: +1; perf harness is already adding metadata artifact uploader. we can reuse fields.

Jonas Weber: re interpretation: we should explicitly say what we *won’t* conclude from sanity suite:
- not enough to claim “no quality regression” broadly
- only blocks obvious breakages / large deltas
- full eval sign-off required to flip defaults in catalog

Olivia Grant: also: if we see small regressions but big perf wins, we can consider gating by workload / opt-in flag instead of default.

Hiro Tanaka: from runtime: if sanity flags a regression, we need a “fast isolate”: is it FP8 attention vs INT8 matmul vs scheduler? can you tag per-kernel-mode + enable knobs so we can bisect quickly?

Priyanka Bose: yep, will run with explicit modes:
- baseline (bf16)
- fp8_attn_only
- int8_matmul_only
- fp8+int8 combo (if supported)

Arjun Desai: awesome. we should align on “fail closed” behavior:
- if sanity run fails (infra), do not auto-approve enablement
- if metrics missing for a model, default stays baseline

Jonas Weber: +1. i’ll write that into the sign-off criteria. for now: sanity suite gates canary enablement beyond 1% cohort.

Claire Dubois: last ask: run each prompt at least 2x for the non-deterministic bucket and report variance. even w/ fixed seeds we’ve seen minor nondeterminism.

Priyanka Bose: ok, bucket B (temp=0.2) will run 2 replicas; bucket A (temp=0) single.

Talia Benson: sounds good. please post link + status in #eng-runtime too so the kernel folks see it.

Jonas Weber: action items:
- Priyanka: draft quant_sanity_v1 prompt list + runner config (today)
- Olivia: define scoring functions for structured/tool + repetition heuristics (today)
- Arjun/Jonas/Claire: finalize thresholds + “what blocks rollout” note (tomorrow AM)

Olivia Grant: i’ll also add a small dashboard snippet to show pass rates over time by kernel_mode. not fancy but something.

EvalBot: Reminder set by Olivia Grant: "quant_sanity_v1 scoring draft" at 2026-02-15 11:00 PT.

Arjun Desai: thx all. once we have first results, we should look specifically at long-context on FP8. i’m worried about the long-context regression report we saw last month.

Jonas Weber: agreed. if FP8 long-context fails sanity for a model, we’ll keep FP8 off for that model until full eval + mitigation (maybe mixed precision for attention at long seq-lens).

Grace Kim: :thumbsup: that matches how we’re thinking about kernel autoselect too (seq-len regime based).

Claire Dubois: ok. please make sure the report is shareable + includes caveats. we’ll likely need to reference internally for ADR + release notes later.

Priyanka Bose: will do. i’ll post first run outputs once I get the model IDs from Grace.
